components.purpose: The cEOS contract as loadable Agent Skills. Members are named one by one rather than declaring the directory, so a ninth skill appearing in the pack is unmanaged and fails the gate - an independent review added one and the first version of this checker reported nothing unmanaged.

decision.rationale: Authored in this repository under E24. Carries no code and no credentials; a skill is prompt text the agent may load.

components.purpose: Security-focused review of a diff, with an adversarial-modeler subagent. Directly relevant to the Python-to-Rust migration, where every change is a differential change.

decision.rationale: Vendor trust; prompt and subagents only.

components.purpose: PreToolUse guard refusing a hand-edit to a generated document at the moment it is attempted. Fails open on anything it cannot parse.

decision.rationale: Authored here, executes only this repository's own shell script, and the CI drift check remains the authority regardless of whether it runs.

components.purpose: Mutation-testing campaigns. The mechanical answer to the question the verifier asks by hand: would these tests have failed against the pre-fix code? E25-S06 depends on this technique.
Property-based tests. Most of the eleven falsification axes are properties rather than examples: unknown never becomes absent, dry-run has no effect, a protected name resists every spelling.
Language-server intelligence for the Python surface: 51 files, 17,919 lines, 27 modules in scripts/ implementing the governance gates.

decision.rationale: First-party marketplace, the symmetric counterpart of rust-analyzer-lsp: the Rust side had a language server and the side holding every gate did not. Carries no prompt content, so it costs nothing in any session. Pyright is code intelligence only - mypy remains the repository's type-check gate, and a Pyright diagnostic is not a gate verdict.

components.purpose: Language-server intelligence for the Rust workspace.

decision.rationale: First-party marketplace. Runs rust-analyzer, which the developer already runs.

components.purpose: Rust security review with a worker/judge pipeline, including a false-positive judge. The highest-value component for this project: review throughput is bounded by rounds, and filtering false positives buys more than another reviewer would.

decision.rationale: Vendor trust. Ships three subagents and no hooks or MCP servers, so it can read and reason but cannot install anything or reach the network on its own.

components.purpose: Checks code against the documents that specify it. This repository has 260 specifying documents and no mechanical link from a requirement to the code that implements it.

decision.rationale: Vendor trust; prompt and one subagent.

components.purpose: CodeQL, Semgrep and SARIF parsing. Complements the repository's own codeql.yml by making the same analyses runnable locally during review.

decision.rationale: Vendor trust. Runs scanner binaries, which is code execution, so it carries the highest capability of the set and the largest always-on cost. Reconsider at the next review if it is not being used.

components.purpose: Dependency supply-chain risk. Serves ADR-0009 and docs/security/SUPPLY_CHAIN.md, and the dependency-ring rules of ADR-0019.
Given one defect, find its variants across the codebase. Automates the lesson of the E00 review history: close the class, not the reported case.

decision.rationale: Trail of Bits is a named security vendor with a public track record. Ships one skill, no hooks, no MCP server: prompt content only.

rejected.reason: Duplicates project/*.json as a second source of truth for planning, without Change Risk Levels or safety gates. A second definition of Done in one repository is the class of defect the E00 review took three rounds to close.

Named personas passing context through files. The executor/verifier split here is stricter because it is bounded and because a CR4 verdict is not the executor's to write. Personas add theatre, not guarantees.
Duplicates scripts/project_os.py without the risk model or the gates.

Not rejected as worthless - four of its patterns were harvested into .claude/skills. Rejected as an installation, because it defines Done its own way and this repository already defines Done more strictly and ties it to safety invariants.

Rule 3 (surgical changes) was harvested into AGENTS.md's Diff discipline. The package is rejected: it is a CLAUDE.md, so it is always resident rather than progressively disclosed, and its rule 2 forbids 'error handling for unrealistic edge cases' - in this product the unrealistic edge cases are the product.

Five lifecycle hooks, an MCP server, a background worker and a default cloud provider that ships session transcripts to cmem.ai. Refused by this manifest's own capability bar (executes-code + network at Community trust), and it would carry exactly what AGENTS.md forbids committing: real transcripts, prompts, source and home paths.

A gateway routing prompts across 352 providers. Refused by the capability bar, and it would falsify the executor/verifier attribution the evidence packets record: a gateway choosing a provider by quota makes 'Codex performed the independent review' unverifiable.

Prompt-only, so it clears the trust bar. Refused on cost and duplication: a 14,460-token body whose own description requires invoking it before the first tool call of every session - 2.4x the whole context budget - and it generates skill edits, which is a second copy of the contract produced without review. The concept was kept as E28-S03.

Not identifiable as a component: at least five unrelated projects share the name, the headroomlabs org publishes no public repository despite an Apache-2.0 claim, and the PyPI package of that name is an unrelated CLI. No source or version could be written into this manifest honestly.

Stands for the whole 'someone else's Claude Code configuration' class, of which the census found at least eight. Same shape as obra/superpowers and multica-ai/andrej-karpathy-skills, both already rejected: a starter CLAUDE.md plus agents, skills and hooks that define the method a second time.

First-party and 176k stars, and refused anyway: the repository carries no licence file and the licence endpoint returns 404, so by default all rights are reserved. This repository maintains a licence allow-list for Rust crates; prompt content it carries into the agent is the same question on a different artifact. E28-S04 makes that check mechanical.
GPL-3.0. Outside any allow-list this repository would accept for content it carries and derives from.

Duplicates scripts/project_os.py - file-based planning with 50 hooks and 353 scripts - without the Change Risk Levels, the risk floors or the gates. Same rejection as github/spec-kit and claude-task-master.

25 method skills and 9 hooks defining spec-driven, test-driven and constraint-driven development. A second definition of how work is done, which AGENTS.md already defines more strictly and ties to Safety Invariants.
358 hooks maintaining state through ledgers and handoffs, and no push since 2026-01-26. The abandonment signal alone disqualifies it; the evidence ledger already answers what it addresses.

A 342-repository census over 22 queries, ranked by stars, run at the owner's request rather than against a named gap. It produced one installation (pyright-lsp) and three stories (E28-S01/S02/S03); the entries above name the candidates judged individually. The classes that carried the rest, so they are not re-derived: catalogues and awesome-lists, which index components rather than being one; packages that define Done or the method a second time; sources with no licence or an incompatible one; domains this product does not touch; upstreams with no push in over six months; and tools duplicating a gate this repository already runs. The headline result is negative and worth keeping: the fourteen most-starred repositories, 1.7 million stars between them, yielded no installable component for this codebase.

license_allowlist_note: Licences admissible for prompt content and tooling this repository carries into the agent. Deliberately not a copy of rust/deny.toml's crate allow-list: that governs linked code, this governs text the agent reads and patterns this repository may derive from. CC-BY-SA-4.0 is admitted because trailofbits/skills is carried under it, and AGENTS.md records harvesting patterns from external packs - share-alike is a condition worth naming rather than discovering.
